reasons: Grouping is lost: the Datadog query is avg by {db}, but the candidate's avg( ) has no by (postgresql_database_name) clause, so it collapses all databases into one series.

Template filters are dropped: $db (prefix db) and $host (prefix host) should become matchers postgresql_database_name=~"$db" and host_name=~"$host", using the observed dataset labels; the candidate applies no matchers at all.

Unit/quantity: the candidate wraps the monotonic sum in rate(...[$__rate_interval]), yielding a per-second rate, while the Datadog query averages the raw rows_deleted value with no rate; the expression needs verification of the Datadog metric's native type before a rate is applied.
postgresql.tup_deleted (rows/tuples deleted) is a reasonable quantity match for postgresql.rows_deleted, so the metric choice itself is acceptable.
The translated outcome is correct because an exact mapping exists, but the produced PromQL does not reproduce the Datadog series set.
